Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

We are moving interview audio and scanned consent forms from the shared intake folder to the center storage server, and I need the profile to be usable by two coordinators without changing their existing folder names. The workstation is called Atlas Desk, and it runs Windows 11. The uploader is already installed, but the current profile points to a retired server, so please make a separate profile rather than editing that one. The new profile should be called Harbor Archive, and it should be visible to both coordinator accounts after they sign in. The profile is for ordinary weekly transfers, not for the public website, and it should leave the local source files in place after a successful upload.

The storage server is Vault North, and the destination folder is /collections/oral-history/intake. The server address is already saved in the credential manager under Harbor Ingest, so use that saved entry and do not ask the coordinators to type a password into the profile. The shared intake folder is D:\archive\ready, and the team keeps dated subfolders inside it. The uploader should scan those subfolders, but it should not flatten them because the year and interview number are part of each record. The archive lead said, “We have had two batches land in the wrong interview folder when a tool flattened the names,” so retain the folder structure and retain the filenames exactly as they are.

Set the maximum number of simultaneous transfers to three because the storage server is shared with the catalog station, and the network team has reserved about 40 megabits per second for this workstation. The coordinators do not need a progress window covering the full screen, but they do want to see the current filename and the number of files remaining. Keep the completed transfer history for 30 days so they can answer questions about a recent delivery, and keep failed items in the list until somebody retries or removes them. The history should not include the contents of the audio or form files.

transfer.allow_resume

Please enable the setting shown on that line so a transfer that loses its connection can continue from the point it stopped instead of starting that file again. The largest audio file in the current collection is about 6 gigabytes, and some scans are much smaller, so the restart behavior matters even when a coordinator is working through a long batch. The server sometimes closes an idle connection after 12 minutes. The network team confirmed that limit last week and asked us to avoid changing it on the server side. The profile should reconnect after a dropped connection and wait 60 seconds before its first retry, then use a longer pause between later retries, but cap the total at five attempts.

The source folder is checked every 15 minutes on weekdays between 7 in the morning and 6 in the evening. Do not start two scans at once. If one scan is still checking dated folders when the next interval arrives, let the current scan finish and then skip that interval rather than building a queue. The coordinators sometimes add a late file at the end of the day, so include a manual scan button as well. The archive lead asked for a quiet notification on completion and a visible warning if any item fails, but no sound because the desk sits near the reading room. The notification should name the profile and give the number of completed and failed files without showing a filename on a shared screen.

1. Keep the source and destination paths in the profile summary so a coordinator can check them before starting a transfer.
2. Show the saved credential entry as Harbor Ingest, but mask the secret and do not offer a reveal button.
3. Leave automatic deletion turned off because the source folder is our working copy until the archive lead checks the delivery.
4. Let a coordinator pause the whole batch and resume it later, and show a confirmation before they cancel a batch that is already sending files. The confirmation should say how many files have finished and how many are still pending. It must not imply that canceling removes anything from the server.

The support technician told me, “If the connection drops during a large interview file, we want the uploader to reconnect and continue that same file when the destination still has the partial upload.” Please preserve that behavior. The retry limit is five attempts in total, not five additional attempts. If the saved credential entry cannot be found, the profile should remain saved, but the uploader should ask the signed-in coordinator to select an available credential before a transfer begins. Do not fall back to an anonymous connection, and do not put the password into a log.

Before the coordinators use this profile, ask the technician to run a test with three sample files: one WAV interview that is larger than one gigabyte and two small consent scans. The samples should come from the test folder rather than the live intake folder, and the test destination should be /sandbox/harbor-check. The test should confirm that the dated subfolder and each filename arrive unchanged. It should also confirm that a paused batch resumes and that a deliberately interrupted connection follows the retry rule. Please make clear in the handoff notes that this is a requested test and has not been run yet.

For the first live week, the coordinators will review the transfer history each afternoon and report any repeated failure to the archive lead. Do not add an automatic email recipient because the center has not chosen one yet. If both coordinator accounts are signed in at the same time, they should still see the same profile settings and separate activity histories. The activity history should identify which account started a batch, but it should not record the credential secret. Keep the settings page straightforward enough that a substitute coordinator can check the schedule and destination without opening the advanced network panel.

One condition matters for the schedule: if the center announces a closure day, the archive lead will tell the coordinators before the previous afternoon, and they should disable that day's scan manually. Do not invent a holiday calendar or assume the uploader can infer closures from the workstation calendar. The weekly schedule otherwise stays in place. If the source folder is empty at a scheduled scan, show a quiet completed notice with zero files found and do not treat that as a failure. Please put the closure note next to the weekday schedule so it is visible during setup.

At the end, please leave the existing retired-server profile untouched and name the new one Harbor Archive exactly as stated. Make the setting labels understandable to the coordinators without changing the filenames or the saved credential name. Include the retry details and the manual scan behavior in the handoff note, and keep the note to the practical setup points above. The technicians need the profile request and its test steps together because they are preparing Atlas Desk for the next intake week. Do not say that the profile has been created or that the test passed, since I am only asking for the configuration and test to be done."}]
